research_question: Does a VCP leader that sustains cross-sectional relative strength throughout its recorded final contraction have more reliable post-breakout follow-through than one that only reaches the RS threshold on the signal day?
mechanism: A genuine leader should absorb supply while its base forms. The final contraction may reduce absolute price, but relative strength should remain persistently high rather than recover only on the breakout bar.
primary_feature: Share of market sessions from the recorded final-leg pivot_date through signal_date whose existing 63/126/252-day composite cross-sectional RS percentile is at least 85.
causal_contract: RS uses only closes available on each evaluated date. The feature window ends on the completed signal date. Future columns are labels only.

population.deduplication: First signal per symbol, scale and pivot_date, sorted by signal_date and symbol.

guardrails.failure_action: Stop RS-window and threshold variants; retain the existing signal-day RS gate and frozen strategy.
guardrails.pass_action: Treat final-leg RS persistence as a supported mechanism for a separately frozen forward candidate; do not tune it on this history.
